steps.stdout:
Create a task in a project.

With --attach this session is attached to the new task as `session attach`
would do it, which is what keeps the new number from having to be carried by
hand to the next command. A title naming a reference an open task already
names refuses the create unless --force is given; a title merely worded like
one is created, with the tasks it resembles reported on stderr.

Usage:
  kaneo task create <title> [flags]

Flags:
      --assignee string           user id to assign
      --attach                    attach this session to the new task, as `session attach` would
  -d, --description string        task description; - reads stdin
      --description-file string   read the description from a file; - reads stdin
      --due-date string           due date
      --force                     create the task even when an open task names the same reference
  -h, --help                      help for create
      --next string               first step to record on the new task; needs --attach
      --priority string           urgent, high, medium, low or no-priority (default medium)
      --start-date string         start date: a date, or a date and time with an offset
      --status string             column slug to create the task in (default to-do)

Global Flags:
      --api-key string     API key; prefer KANEO_API_KEY, since a flag is visible in the process list
      --api-url string     Kaneo base URL (env KANEO_API_URL)
      --human              force human-readable output, even through a pipe
      --jq string          filter JSON output with a jq expression (implies --json)
      --json               force JSON output
  -p, --project string     project id, slug or name (env KANEO_PROJECT)
      --timeout duration   per-request timeout (default 10s)
  -w, --workspace string   workspace id, slug or name (env KANEO_WORKSPACE)
